svg.title: The flow of a parametrized test: one decorated function enters collection, pytest pairs each case with the function body to create independent test items with their own ids, then runs each item through its own arrange, act and assert phases with fresh fixtures, and reports each one separately so a single failing case does not hide the results of the others
svg.text: One function in, N independent tests out
the expansion happens at collection time, before a single assertion runs
1. What you write — one decorator, one body
@pytest.mark.parametrize(("ref", "topic", "minutes"), CASES, ids=NAMES)
def test_refuses_a_bad_value(ref, topic, minutes):
the decorator supplies the arguments; the body never sees a loop
2. Collection — pytest pairs every case with the body
six tuples of values plus one function become six separate test items
each item gets an id: the function name plus the label from ids=
see it without running anything: pytest --collect-only -q
3. Six independent items, each with its own name
...bad_value[ref-without-prefix]
...bad_value[ref-too-short]
...bad_value[topic-not-lower-case]
...bad_value[topic-padded]
...bad_value[minutes-zero]
...bad_value[minutes-over-the-cap]
4. Each item runs alone: fresh fixtures, arrange, act, assert, teardown
a function-scoped fixture is built again for every one of the six
nothing one case does can be seen by the next
5. Reported one by one: 1 failed, 38 passed — the failure names [minutes-zero], the other five still ran
